mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: doorganize() for the extended command 'adjust' is not ported

summary: invent.c owns the #adjust boundary: doorganize() selects an inventory source object with getobj("adjust", ...), then doorganize_core() asks for a destination letter and performs collect, move, merge, swap, or split bookkeeping. At the refreshed stop, the C recording has just painted What do you want to adjust? [a-km or ?*] after #adjust; JavaScript has the adjust and altadjust rows plus item-action queue wiring, but js/cmd.js doextcmd() lacks doorganize and adjust_split cases and falls into its generic refusal before invent.js getobj() runs. Port the complete invent.c adjust family and wire both handlers, preserving inventory-chain ordering, object names, messages, redraw, cancellation, malformed-gold handling, and split/count paths.

source.branch: doorganize() returns ECMD_OK with a no-adjustable message only for an empty inventory or a sole gold stack already in '$'; otherwise !fixinv first reassigns letters, check_invent_gold("adjust") selects a filter that excludes ordinary gold or admits malformed gold, and getobj("adjust", filter, GETOBJ_PROMPT | GETOBJ_ALLOWCNT) chooses the source. doorganize_core() then accepts cancel, same-letter collection, a different destination for move/merge/swap, or a counted split; adjust_split() is the internal item-action path for non-gold stacks of at least two and validates a split count before calling splitobj(). The assigned recording has the normal fixed-letter path, a named long sword in slot a, and destination z, with no RNG at the boundary.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1673-1674 binds the M-a/adjust extended-command row to doorganize(); js/extcmdlist_data.js:45 already preserves that row, while js/cmd.js:4885-5150 has no doorganize case and reaches its default refusal.

nethack-c/upstream/src/iactions.c:191-197 queues doorganize or adjust_split followed by the selected inventory letter; js/iactions.js:295-302 mirrors both queues, so the same production handlers must serve item-actions.
nethack-c/upstream/src/invent.c:4981-5003 is the user entrypoint and :5008-5064 is the internal split entrypoint; both converge on :5068-5279 doorganize_core().
dependencies: invent.c:4889-4913 check_invent_gold(), :739-765 reorder_invent(), and reassign() provide gold validation, inventory ordering, and !fixinv relabeling; js/invent.js already has check_invent_gold(), reassign(), and the equivalent private reorderInventory().

doorganize_core() uses invent.c mergable()/merged(), extract_nobj(), inv_cnt(), assigninvlet(), clear_splitobjs(), prinv(), and update_inventory(); the existing JS ports are js/invent.js, js/obj.js, and js/hack.js, but their state and message ordering must be preserved while wiring the new owner.

The destination ?/* branch calls invent.c:3467-3518 display_used_invlets(), which paints a selectable Inventory letters used menu and returns a letter or cancel; no display_used_invlets owner exists in js/invent.js, so this return-valued dependency is part of the source-general scope.

The GETOBJ_ALLOWCNT source branch at invent.c:1937-1947 and adjust_split() at :5022-5040 consume get_count(); js/invent.js:832-843 currently raises UnsupportedObjectPromptError for get_count() and splitobj(), so counted adjust and the internal stack-split path need explicit completion or a recorded dependency handoff.

C defers prinv() and update_inventory() until the inventory chain has been restored (:5262-5279); js/invent.js:3267-3283 and :1727-1740 provide those output/refresh seams, while object names and merge side effects flow through the existing object and inventory modules.
